Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

18*3256-1980 

Indian Standard 

CODE FOR INLAND PACKAGING OF 
ROPES AND CORDAGES 



( First Revision ) 



0. FOREWORD 

0.1 This Indian Standard ( First Revision ) was adopted by the Indian 
Standards Institution on 4 June 1980, after the draft finalized by the 
Cordages Sectional Committee had been approved by the Textile 
Division Council. 

0*2 Packaging plays a very important part in preventing damage in 
handling and in the safe transport of goods, as also in their storage and 
marketing. Proper packaging with satisfactory quality of packing 
materials also preserves the contents from infestation, contamination and 
other deterioration. This code gives details of packaging of ropes and 
cordages intended for home consumption. 

0*3 This standard was originally published in 1965 In this revision, 
besides other modifications, use of hessian has been specified in place of 
heavy cee cloth for the outer layer of packing. 

0.4 In formulating this standard, assistance has been derived from the 
* Defence services packing code ' issued by the Ministry of Defence, 
Government of India. 



1. SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes requirements for packing of textile ropes and 
cordages intended for home consumption. 

2. PACKING 

2*1 Ropes and Lines 

2.1.1 Each coil of specified length and size shall be tied at 4 places 
with a line or cord of adequate strength to allow the coil to hang by any 
one tie. 



IS: 3256- 1989 



2.1.2 The specified number of coils shall be wrapped with sufficient 
overlap in either of the following combinations:

Inner layer 
Middle layer 
Outer layer 



Combination B 

Inner layer 

Outer layer 



40 pm low density polyethylene him 

(see IS: 2508-1977*) 
Waterproof packing paper conforming: 

to Type 1 of IS : l398-1968f 

245 to 305 g/m 2 hessian [see IS : 2818 
(PartI)-1971J], 
IS: 2818 (.Part II)-1971t, 
IS: 2818 (Part III J-1971J, 
IS: 2818 (PartIV)-1971J,

40 |Jtrn low density polyethylene film 

(see IS: 2508-1977*) 
245 to 305 g/m* hessian [see IS : 2818 

(Part I)-1971J, 

IS: 2818 (PartII)-1971){, 

IS: 2818 (Part III )-1971t, 

IS: 2818 (PartIV)-197l^ 

IS: 2818 (Part V)-1974t, 

IS: 2818 (PartVI)-1977J] 



2.K3 The hessian layer shall be hand-sewn With two strands of 3-ply 
jute twine of adequate strength, maintaining about 20 stitches per metre. 
The inner layers of wrapping material shall not get pierced during 
sewing. 



♦Specification for low density polyethylene films (first revision ), 

fSpecification for packing paper, waterproof, bitumen-laminated (first revision ). 

^Specification for Indian hessian: 

Part I General ( first revision ) . 

Part II 305 and 229 g/m« at 16 percent contract regain (first revision ). 

Part III 213 and 270 g/m2 at 16 percent contract regain. 

Part IV 213 and 270 g/m* at 14 percent contract regain. 

Part V 298 g/m.2 a t 16 percent contract regain. 

Part VI 245 g/m.2 at 16 percent contract regain. 



IS: 3256 -1980 

2.2 Cords and Twines 

2.2.1 The specified number of hanks or skeins of cords and twines shall 
be made into rectangular packages of mass not exceeding that specified in 
the relevant specification. 

2.2.2 The bundles made as in 2.2.1 shall be wrapped in either of the 
combinations mentioned in 2.1.2 and the outer layer sewn as in 2.1.3. 

3. PACKING MATERIALS 

3.1 The packing materials shall be in sound, clean and dry condition 
and shall be of sufficient size to cover the contents with adequate over- 
laps on all sides.
